dimensions.assessment_basis: The preserved sources establish the bounded consequence described in the Incident summary: Google paused Gemini's generation of images of people after users surfaced historically inaccurate and offensive outputs. Google later explained that diversity tuning failed to account for contexts where diversity should not be introduced and that the model also became more cautious than intended, refusing some benign prompts. Unreported downstream consequences were not inferred. Threshold applied: Material disruption of an important service or organisational workflow; a critical or important function unavailable for more than two hours; complete relevant cloud-service unavailability over 30 minutes; or limited availability affecting over five percent or one million EU users, whichever is smaller, for over one hour, with bounded recovery.

aggregate_harm_screening.rationale: This review assesses the particular reported occurrence and its bounded consequences, including evidence-limited alleged consequences. Public reach does not establish lifecycle deployment. No model-wide audience or separate Aggregate Harm score is imported.

public_interpretation_before: A protective and diversity-oriented control became operative in contexts where its valid conditions were not satisfied and also over-triggered refusals on benign requests. This is a strong example of a safeguard/tuning objective activating outside its appropriate scope. Inappropriate triggering is distinct from control nonactivation. Pausing and proposed changes are response evidence, without proof of restored calibration. Later GAI Profile, development Profile and EU requirements are not retrospective, and standalone image generation is not runtime-agent dispatch. The provider’s pause is Aligned with the AI RMF disengagement requirement. The pause does not establish repaired generation quality.

factual_basis_before: Google states that its tuning to produce diverse people did not correctly distinguish historical or otherwise specific contexts and that the model overcompensated. Google temporarily disabled people-image generation and committed to further testing. AIID Incident 645 aggregates 35 reports around the same failure cluster.
factual_basis_after: Google states that its tuning to produce diverse people did not correctly distinguish historical or otherwise specific contexts and that the model overcompensated. Google temporarily disabled people-image generation and committed to further testing. AIID Incident 645 aggregates 35 reports around the same failure cluster. Google’s 28 August 2024 update describes a staged rollout of renewed people-image generation with Imagen 3. This bounds the period of withdrawn functionality without proving universal restoration or repaired calibration.
decisive_reasoning: Google withdrew the live people-image generation function and described a staged replacement months later. The actual loss of this product function supports material bounded service impairment. It was not an essential service, and elapsed months alone do not support S4. Google acknowledged and apologised for offensive/inaccurate portrayals. This supports an attributable correction and bounded dignitary affront. A distinct material loss of standing or opportunity is not substantiated.
